# Skill: Jenkins Deployment Strategies

## Implementation Rules:
- **[ARCHITECTURE]** Build once, deploy many: the image is built only once in the CI stage, pushed, and identified by its `sha256` digest (`$IMAGE_REPO@$IMAGE_DIGEST`); dev, staging, and prod receive the same digest and only the configuration changes (per-environment values).
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Rebuilding the artifact or image per environment, deploying by mutable tag (`:latest`, `:develop`, `:staging`), using `--set image.tag=latest`, or checking out another branch for the production deploy: the artifact in prod would not be the one that was tested.
- **[MANDATORY]** The digest is read from the builder output (BuildKit's `--metadata-file` or Kaniko's `--digest-file`) with `readJSON`/`readFile`, saved in `env.IMAGE_REF`, archived with `archiveArtifacts artifacts: 'image-digest.txt', fingerprint: true`, and reported in `currentBuild.description`.
- **[PATTERN]** Promotion with dedicated, sequential stages: automatic `Deploy staging` on `main` after the quality gates, `Approve prod`, and `Deploy prod`; every deploy stage has `when { beforeAgent true; branch 'main' }` (or `buildingTag()`) and its own pod with the environment's ServiceAccount.
- **[MANDATORY]** Approvals with the stage-level `input` directive (`message`, `ok`, `submitter 'payments-release-managers'`, `submitterParameter 'APPROVER'`) in a stage without an agent (top-level `agent none`) and with `options { timeout(time: 4, unit: 'HOURS') }`: the wait occupies no executor or pod and expires explicitly.
- **[MANDATORY]** `milestone(ordinal: 20, label: 'prod-approved')` with increasing ordinals before the deploy and right after each approval: when a newer build passes a milestone, older builds that have not yet reached it are aborted, and an older build cannot pass a milestone already passed by a newer one; never `milestone` inside `parallel`.
- **[MANDATORY]** `options { lock(resource: 'payments-api-staging', inversePrecedence: true) }` on deploy stages to serialize access to the environment, with `milestone` inside the lock so the most recent build always wins; resources declared in JCasC under `unclassified.lockableResourcesManager.declaredResources`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `disableConcurrentBuilds(abortPrevious: true)` in release pipelines: it interrupts an in-progress `helm upgrade`, leaving the release in `pending-upgrade` state; concurrency on `main` is governed with `milestone` and `lock`.
- **[PATTERN]** Atomic Helm deploy: `helm upgrade --install payments-api ./chart --namespace payments-staging -f chart/values-staging.yaml --set image.ref="$IMAGE_REF" --atomic --wait --timeout 10m --history-max 10 --description "commit $GIT_COMMIT build $BUILD_NUMBER"` (with Helm 4 the equivalent of `--atomic` is `--rollback-on-failure`); the chart references the image by digest.
- **[PATTERN]** Smoke tests after every deploy (`helm test payments-api -n payments-staging --logs --timeout 5m` and `curl --fail --retry 10 --retry-all-errors` on the readiness endpoint) in a separate stage, with automatic rollback in `post { failure { } }`: `helm rollback payments-api 0 -n payments-staging --wait` or `kubectl rollout undo deployment/payments-api -n payments-staging`.
- **[PATTERN]** In production prefer progressive strategies: canary with Argo Rollouts or Flagger (metrics-driven promotion) or blue-green with two releases (`payments-api-blue`, `payments-api-green`) and a switch of the Service selector only after smoke tests pass.
- **[PATTERN]** GitOps alternative: the pipeline does not access the production cluster but updates the digest in the manifests repository (`yq -i '.image.ref = strenv(IMAGE_REF)' envs/prod/payments-api/values.yaml`), pushes to a branch with `gitUsernamePassword`, and opens a PR; Argo CD or Flux sync after the merge, which constitutes the approval.
- **[SECURITY]** Separate deploy credentials per environment and least privilege: the deploy pod's ServiceAccount with a `RoleBinding` on the target namespace only, dedicated Kubernetes clouds or folders for prod; no prod deploys from PR builds or from branches other than `main` or release tags.
- **[SECURITY]** Verify the artifact before promotion: sign the digest with cosign (`cosign sign --key k8s://jenkins-agents/cosign-key "$IMAGE_REF"`) in the CI stage and run `cosign verify --key k8s://jenkins-agents/cosign-key "$IMAGE_REF"` before the prod deploy, with an admission policy (Kyverno/Gatekeeper) that accepts only signed images from the internal registry.
- **[PATTERN]** End-to-end traceability: OCI labels `org.opencontainers.image.revision`/`source`/`version` on the image, `app.kubernetes.io/version` and `acme.it/git-commit` annotations on resources, `--description` in Helm, `currentBuild.displayName` with the version, approver recorded by `submitterParameter`, and a changelog from `git log --oneline "$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)"..HEAD` archived with the build.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Versioned per-environment values (`chart/values-dev.yaml`, `values-staging.yaml`, `values-prod.yaml`) without secrets (External Secrets or Sealed Secrets); across environments only configuration, replicas, resources, and URLs change, never the code.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** The release pipeline's top-level `timeout` includes the approval window (e.g. `timeout(time: 6, unit: 'HOURS')` with a 4-hour approval) and every deploy stage has its own tight `timeout`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `input` as a step inside a stage with an agent, inside `container()` or `node`; `input` without `submitter` or without `timeout`; concurrent deploys to the same environment without `lock`; `kubectl apply` without rollout verification.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Promotion without recompilation or a full checkout: copy the digest between separate registries with `skopeo copy` or `crane copy` preserving the digest, chart published as OCI (`helm upgrade --install payments-api oci://harbor.acme.internal/charts/payments-api --version 1.4.2`), `stash` limited to the chart and `image-digest.txt`.
- **[TESTING]** Every deploy is verified automatically: `kubectl rollout status deployment/payments-api -n payments-staging --timeout=5m` or Helm's `--wait`, smoke tests, E2E tests in staging before prod approval, and periodic rollback drills in staging.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `EXAMPLES.md` in this folder for reference anti-patterns and best practices.
